storage.value:
BP-4 Billing procedure — half-hourly business accounts

Version 7 · 21 September 2026 · Owner: Imogen Ashdale (Billing Manager). This procedure governs every billing run of the Business Half-Hourly (BHH) book. Where a handbook, a trial sheet or a customer copy differs from it, this procedure and the records it names govern.

1. Scope and period

1.1 A run bills every BHH account with any supply in the run period. The run period is a span of UK civil days (BR-2611: 15 October to 14 November 2026 inclusive).

2. What is charged

2.1 Unit charges are priced on the active energy consumed at the metering point in each half-hour settlement period, attributed to the half-hour in which it was consumed, and banded by the time-of-use bands.

2.2 The capacity charge is priced on demand: the average power drawn over a half-hour (kW), that is the half-hour's active energy in kWh multiplied by two. See "Capacity and excess reactive charges — method".

2.3 The excess reactive charge is priced on reactive energy (kvarh) half-hour by half-hour, as the method page sets out.

2.4 The standing charge is charged for each day on supply.

3. Tariff editions

3.1 Each half-hour is priced at the tariff edition in force when its energy was consumed, as each edition's page states. The date of the bill does not decide the edition (internal audit 2026-H1, finding 1).

3.2 Where a run period spans two editions, every charge is worked separately for the part of the period each edition covers and appears once per edition on the draft.

4. Time

4.1 Time-of-use bands and edition dates are written in UK civil time. The civil day of a half-hour (for its band, its edition, the supply dates and standing-charge days) is the UK civil date on which the half-hour begins.

5. Supply dates

5.1 Only half-hours on days the site was on supply are billed: from the Supply start date on the site account (or the first day of the run period, whichever is later) to its Supply end date, the last day on supply (or the last day of the run period, whichever is earlier), inclusive.

5.2 A Supply end date after the run period does not shorten the run period.

6. Sources of record

WhatRecord
TariffThe edition pages in this space (rates, the consumption each edition covers).
Site and supplyThe site Account in the CRM: supply start and end, ledger customer, billing contact.
MeterThe metering asset register (Notion): one page per meter; the page body is the meter's commissioning record (installation, measurement transformers, programming, data retrieval). The meter profiles table in the Metering Operations base lists each meter's collector and the export its data arrive in.
Interval dataThe collectors' exports for the run as delivered to the run folder, in the format each collector's data collection agreement sets (agreements filed in Box under Metering / Data collection agreements).
LedgerQuickBooks. Xero is the pre-2026 archive and is read-only.

7. Quantities and rounding

7.1 Sum each band's energy for each edition part at full precision and round the billed quantity half up to 0.001 kWh. Excess reactive energy is rounded half up to 0.001 kvarh. Maximum demand is rounded half up to 0.01 kW.

7.2 Standing charge = days on supply in the edition part × the daily rate. Capacity charge = maximum demand × days on supply in the edition part × the rate. Unit and reactive charges = billed quantity × rate.

7.3 Each line amount is converted to pounds and rounded half up to the penny. A draft's net total is the sum of its line amounts.

8. Drafts

8.1 One draft invoice per site in QuickBooks, against the ledger customer the site Account names; invoice date 16 November 2026, due 30 November 2026.

8.2 One line per charge per edition. The line description is "<charge name> (Edition <n>)" with the charge name exactly as the charge schedule names it: Standing charge, Peak unit charge, Day unit charge, Night unit charge, Capacity charge, Excess reactive charge. The line Amount is the charge in pounds, net of VAT. A line whose amount is zero may be left off.

8.3 To correct a draft, void your own draft and create a new one.

9. Summary mail

9.1 When every draft of the run exists, send one mail to the Billing Manager with the subject "BR-yymm drafts ready: <number of drafts> invoices, £<sum of the drafts' net totals, two decimals>".

10. What analysts do not do

10.1 Analysts do not send, issue, authorise or collect invoices, do not change meter readings or meter records, and do not contact customers during a run.

Capacity and excess reactive charges — method

Capacity charge

Demand in a half-hour (kW) = the half-hour's active energy (kWh) × 2. The maximum demand of an edition part is the highest half-hour demand among the half-hours of that part on supply. Capacity charge = maximum demand (kW, 0.01) × days on supply in the part × the edition's rate.

Excess reactive charge

In each half-hour, excess reactive energy = the half-hour's reactive energy (kvarh) minus 0.33 × the same half-hour's active energy (kWh), where that is positive, and nil otherwise. The excess of the half-hours of an edition part is summed, rounded to 0.001 kvarh and charged at that edition's rate. A good power factor over the month does not offset a poor one in particular half-hours; the monthly-average method of Editions 1–3 was withdrawn in 2024.

# Billing team handbook — business half-hourly accounts (extract)

Owner: Imogen Ashdale · last reviewed 2 Sep 2026

## 1. What a billing run is
A run (BR-yymm) bills every half-hourly business account on the BHH tariff for one period of local civil days,
normally the 15th of one month to the 14th of the next. The analyst drafts one invoice per site in the ledger;
the Billing Manager approves the drafts; Credit Control issues them and collects by direct debit. Analysts never
issue, authorise or collect.

## 2. Where things are
- Method and sources of record: BP-4 in the Billing & Tariffs space. Where this handbook and BP-4 differ, BP-4
  governs.
- Tariff editions: one page per edition in the same space.
- Site accounts: the CRM (supply dates, ledger customer, billing contact).
- Meters: the metering operations base (meter profiles, collector deliveries) and the metering asset register.
- Interval data: the collector exports for the run, delivered to the run folder.
- Ledger: QuickBooks. Xero holds history before 2026 and is read-only.

## 3. Habits that have saved us
- Read the account before you bill it: supply dates move.
- Never key a figure from last month's run into this month's; the rates and the calendar change.
- Keep the line names exactly as BP-4 gives them; Credit Control's posting rules key on them.
- When a number looks odd, find the record that explains it; do not smooth it.
- Do not contact customers from the billing mailbox during a run. Queries go to the account manager.

## 4. Approvals
The Billing Manager wants one summary mail per run once every draft exists, with the subject line BP-4 gives.

This schedule is the customer copy. The tariff pages in the Billing & Tariffs space are the edition of record;
each edition page states the consumption it covers.

# BR-2611 scope (Billing Manager)

- Accounts: every half-hourly business account on the BHH tariff with any supply in 15 Oct – 14 Nov 2026. There
  are 22 this run: the 21 from BR-2610 plus Brookhay Brewery Taproom.
- Period: local civil days 15 October to 14 November 2026 inclusive.
- Collectors: Harrowmere AMR, Kestrel Data Services, Varden Metering Services. Exports are in the run folder.
- Ledger: QuickBooks drafts only. The Xero organisation is the pre-2026 archive and must not be used.
- Output: the 22 drafts and one summary mail to the Billing Manager. Approval on 17 November.

# The capacity charge — how it is worked out (BHH)

The capacity charge pays for the network capacity your site uses at its busiest. It is set from your maximum
demand: the highest average power, in kW, that your site drew over any single half-hour.

- Demand in a half-hour (kW) is the energy used in that half-hour (kWh) divided by half an hour, i.e. kWh × 2.
- The maximum demand is taken separately within the days each tariff edition covers in the bill, and that edition's
  rate (pence per kW per day) is applied to it for the number of those days that the site was on supply.
- Maximum demand is stated in kW to two decimal places.

Example: a highest half-hour of 61.5 kWh is a maximum demand of 123.00 kW. At 4.800 p/kW/day over 17 days the
charge is 123.00 × 17 × £0.048 = £100.37.

# Reactive power and your bill — customer guidance (BHH)

Motors, compressors and fluorescent lighting draw reactive power as well as active power. Your meter records
both: active energy in kWh and reactive energy in kvarh. The ratio between them is your power factor.

How the excess reactive charge works
- We look at each half-hour separately. In any half-hour where your reactive energy is more than 33 per cent of
  your active energy in that same half-hour, the reactive energy above that 33 per cent is "excess".
- Excess reactive energy is added up over the bill (separately for each tariff edition the bill covers) and
  charged per kvarh.
- A good average power factor over the month does not cancel the excess in the half-hours where it was poor.

Reducing it
Power-factor correction capacitors, variable-speed drives and maintenance of motor loads typically bring the
ratio under 33 per cent. Our energy services team can survey your site.

# VAT, levies and presentation on BHH drafts

- Drafts are net. VAT at the business rate and the Climate Change Levy are added by Credit Control's posting rules
  when a draft is approved and issued; never add them as lines.
- Amounts are in pounds sterling to the penny.
- The invoice date of a BR-2611 draft is 16 November 2026 and its due date 30 November 2026 (direct debit customers
  are collected from 1 December).
- One draft per site. If an analyst has to correct a draft, void it and create a new one; never edit an issued
  invoice.
- The summary total in the run mail is the sum of the drafts' net totals.

VMS-DCA-2026  DATA COLLECTION AGREEMENT  -  SCHEDULE 3
HALF-HOURLY DATA FILE SPECIFICATION  (version 3.1, effective 1 September 2026)
Between Varden Metering Services Ltd and Harrowmere Energy Co-operative

3.1  Delivery. One comma-separated file per delivery, named varden-sched3-<client>-<yyyymmdd>.csv, with a header row.
     Deliveries carry two hours of settlement periods before and after the requested range.

3.2  Columns
     MPAN         the supply number, no spaces
     MSN          the meter serial number

                  settlement systems use the period-ending convention for every client: the period running from
                  00:00 to 00:30 UTC is stamped 0030, and the last period of a UTC day (23:30 to 24:00) is stamped
                  0000 of the following day.
     AI           active import energy in the period, kWh, three decimals
     RI           reactive import energy in the period, kvarh, three decimals
     FLAG         0 actual, 1 estimated, 2 substituted

3.3  Clocks. All timestamps are UTC. Varden does not convert to local time and does not shift for British Summer Time.
     A local day with a clock change is simply 46 or 50 consecutive UTC periods.

3.4  Validation. Varden validates each period against the meter's cumulative register before delivery and flags any
     estimate or substitution in FLAG.

3.5  Changes to this schedule require 60 days' written notice and a new version number.

# Harrowmere AMR — half-hourly export format (in-house collection)

Owner: Data Collection (Bertrand Ilsley). Applies to files named `amr-hh-export-*.csv` produced by the in-house
automatic meter reading (AMR) head-end. Other collectors deliver in their own formats under their data
collection agreements; this note does not describe them.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| site_ref | Harrowmere site reference (HMS-nnnn) as held on the site account |
| msn | meter serial number |
| period_start_utc | UTC instant at which the half-hour settlement period BEGINS (ISO 8601, `Z`) |
| kwh | active import energy in the period, kWh, three decimals |
| kvarh | reactive import energy in the period, kvarh, three decimals |
| read_status | A = actual read retrieved from the meter, E = estimated by the head-end |

Notes
1. The head-end clock is UTC all year. It does not observe British Summer Time; a local-time view has to be
   derived when a rule is written in civil time.
2. Each run's export carries a margin of a few hours before and after the billing period so that late
   periods are not cut off. The margin rows are not part of the billing period.
3. A site that joins or leaves supply part-way through a period is exported for every period the head-end
   could read. Whether a period is billable is decided by the site account, not by the export.
4. Values are as read from the meter. The meter applies the CT ratio it is programmed with (recorded in its
   commissioning record); the head-end applies no multiplier of its own.
5. File checksums are posted to the collector deliveries table in the metering operations base.

final_message:
BR-2611 is drafted: 22 draft invoices are in QuickBooks, one per site, against each site's ledger customer, and one summary mail has gone to Imogen Ashdale. Run net total £286,186.15 (VAT is added at posting). Nothing was sent to a customer, authorised or collected, and no meter reading or meter record was changed.
Total billed energy: 1,143,171.216 kWh — 629,534.629 kWh under Edition 6 and 513,636.587 kWh under Edition 7.
Editions: each half-hour is priced at the edition in force when its energy was consumed (BP-4 section 3), not by the invoice date. Edition 6 covers consumption up to 24:00 on 31 October 2026 and Edition 7 consumption from 00:00 on 1 November 2026, UK civil time, so every invoice carries both editions: 17 days (15–31 October) under Edition 6 and 14 days (1–14 November) under Edition 7 for a site on supply throughout. Dorian's trial sheet, which priced the whole run on Edition 7 because the bills are issued after 1 November (and banded on the UTC timestamps), was not followed; nor was the Edition 6 customer copy in the run folder.
Clock change: the exports are in UTC, and the bands are in UK civil time. Until 01:00 UTC on Sunday 25 October the UK was on BST (UTC+1), so every half-hour before then was moved one hour later before banding; after it, UK time equals UTC. 25 October had 50 half-hours (a 25-hour day): the hour 01:00–02:00 happened twice and both were Night. A half-hour takes its band, edition and day from the UK civil time at which it begins.
Demand-registered meters: the commissioning records in the metering asset register show that the A+ and R+ channels of Ashgrove Plastics Moulding, Fenwick Lane Data Hall, Gorsebrook Laundry Services, Kittering Foods Packing are programmed for the capacity-monitoring service to record the MEAN DEMAND over each half-hour (kW and kvar), not energy. Their export values were therefore halved to get kWh and kvarh (energy = mean demand × 0.5 h), and the values themselves are the half-hour demand in kW for the capacity charge. The metering platform's register advance over the period agrees with the halved recorded figures.
Hollin Bridge Sawmill and Wexcombe Craft Studios are collected by the same collector (Kestrel) on the same meter model, but their commissioning records say their channels record energy (neither has the capacity-monitoring programming), so their values were not halved (Hollin Bridge's were then scaled by its CT correction, below).
Period-ending stamps: Varden Metering Services stamps each half-hour at its END (VMS-DCA-2026 Schedule 3, also in each meter's commissioning record). For Lanyon Quay Fish Market, Merrowby Care Home, Netherfold Veterinary Hospital, Orchard Rise Hotel, Penhallow Tool Hire, Ravensworth Bowls Club every value was attributed to the half-hour before its stamp, so the bands, the 1 November edition boundary and the period's first and last half-hours all moved by one half-hour compared with reading the stamp as the start. The in-house AMR and Kestrel exports stamp the period start.
CT changes: once the run was nearly drafted, the commissioning records of Quenby Print Works, Thornaby Wharf Cold Store, Ashgrove Plastics Moulding, Hollin Bridge Sawmill in the metering asset register carried a 16 November 2026 amendment from the field engineer's site visit (also reported in his note in the field team's Commissioning channel): the DNO replaced the CTs in its HV metering units during the East Harrowmere primary works on 6 October 2026, before the run period began, and those meters are still programmed for their old CT ratios. Everything they recorded over this period, the export values and the platform's register advance included, is therefore understated by old ratio / new ratio, so each was billed on its recorded values multiplied by new ratio / old ratio: Quenby Print Works × 600/300; Thornaby Wharf Cold Store × 400/300; Ashgrove Plastics Moulding × 750/600; Hollin Bridge Sawmill × 600/400. The factor applies to active and reactive values alike, so energy, maximum demand and excess reactive all scale with it. For a demand-registered meter it comes on top of the halving: Ashgrove Plastics Moulding's exported values are half-hour mean demand, so its energy = exported value × 0.5 × 750/600 (× 0.625). The drafts already raised for these sites were voided and replaced by corrected drafts.
Marlpit Garden Centre was billed only from 15 October to 5 November (22 days) because its supply ended: the site account's Supply end date (last day on supply) is 5 November 2026, the new supplier taking over from 00:00 on the next day; the interval data outside those days were not billed.
Brookhay Brewery Taproom was billed only from 22 October to 14 November (24 days) because its supply started on 22 October 2026 (site account Supply start date); the interval data outside those days were not billed.
Wendle Street Offices has a future Supply end date (31 December 2026); that does not shorten this period, so it was billed for the full 31 days.
Capacity charge: for each edition part, the maximum half-hour demand (the billed kWh of the half-hour × 2, which on the demand-registered meters is the corrected recorded kW) within that part, to 0.01 kW, × the days on supply in the part × the edition's rate.
Excess reactive charge: worked half-hour by half-hour — reactive energy above 0.33 × the same half-hour's kWh — summed per edition part; not on the period's average power factor (Dorian's monthly-PF suggestion was not used).
Rounding: kWh and kvarh to 0.001, kW to 0.01, each line amount rounded half up to the penny; a draft's total is the sum of its lines. Lines are named '<charge name> (Edition <n>)'; zero lines were left off.
Ledger customers: each draft went to the customer the site account names; for example the Thornaby Wharf draft went to the active 'Thornaby Wharf Cold Store Ltd' customer, not to the inactive look-alike 'Thornaby Wharf Cold Stores (2019) Ltd', and the 'Orchard Rise Hotels Group' parent account was not used for the Orchard Rise Hotel site.
